extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent examiners, patent practitioners, and applicants
extracted.subtask_short: USPTO patent application form and fees
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and examiner guidance from the MPEP concerning fees/refunds, claim/amendment fee calculations, specification content and formatting, paper requirements, language/translation, and read-only optical disc submission procedures for U.S. patent applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee calculation for amendments and claims
rubrics_metrics.description: The additional fees, if any, due with an amendment are calculated on the basis of the claims (total and independent) which would be present, if the amendment were entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An amendment of a claim (unless it changes a dependent claim to an independent claim or adds to the number of claims referred to in a multiple dependent claim) and replacement of a claim by a claim of the same type do not require additional fees. For fee purposes a claim is treated as dependent if it contains reference to one or more other claims. Any claim in dependent form that is not a proper dependent claim (e.g., does not include every limitation of the claim on which it depends) will be required to be canceled, and further claims depending on it will likewise be required to be canceled. Applicant may amend to place claims in proper dependent form or redraft as independent claims upon payment of any necessary additional fee. Unentered claims will not be counted when calculating the fee due in subsequent amendments. The additional fees due with an amendment are required prior to any consideration of the amendment by the examiner. Money paid for a proposed amendment is not refunded by reason of nonentry of the amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-electronic filing fee and non-DOCX fee
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 10(h) of Public Law 112-29 established an additional fee for each application for an original patent not filed by electronic means (except design, plant, or provisional applications) (see 37 CFR 1.16(t)). For applications filed on or after January 17, 2024 under 35 U.S.C. 111, when filed non-electronically the fee for not conforming to USPTO requirements for submission in DOCX format is also applicable (see 37 CFR 1.16(u)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The non-electronic filing fee applies to applications filed other than via the USPTO patent electronic filing system; see 37 CFR citations. The non-DOCX fee applies where applicable as of the cited dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of insufficient/unspecified payments (nonprovisional)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a payment submitted for the fees due on filing in a nonprovisional application under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) is insufficient and the applicant has not specified the fees to which the payment is to be applied, the Office will apply the payment in the following order until the payment is expended:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ordered application: (1) the basic filing fee (37 CFR 1.16(a),(b),(c), or (e)); (2) the non-electronic filing fee (37 CFR 1.16(t)); (3) the non-DOCX fee (37 CFR 1.16(u)); (4) the application size fee (37 CFR 1.16(s)); (5) the late filing surcharge (37 CFR 1.16(f)); (6) the processing fee for an application filed in a language other than English (37 CFR 1.17(i)); (7) the search fee (37 CFR 1.16(k)-(n)); (8) the examination fee (37 CFR 1.16(o)-(r)); and (9) the excess claims fee (37 CFR 1.16(h)-(j)). The Office will treat a deposit account authorization to charge “the basic filing fee” as authorization to charge basic filing, search, and examination fees unless specifically limited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of insufficient/unspecified payments (provisional)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a payment submitted for the fees due on filing in a provisional application under 35 U.S.C. 111(b) is insufficient and the applicant has not specified the fees to which the payment is to be applied, the Office will apply the payment in the following order until the payment is expended:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ordered application for provisionals: (1) the basic filing fee (37 CFR 1.16(d)); (2) the application size fee (37 CFR 1.16(s)); and (3) the late filing surcharge (37 CFR 1.16(g)). See MPEP § 509 for related deposit/account guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: General refund eligibility (37 CFR 1.26)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may refund any fee paid by mistake or any amount paid in excess of that required (37 CFR 1.26). A change of purpose after payment (e.g., withdrawing a filing) will not entitle a party to a refund of such fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office will not refund amounts of $25 or less unless a refund is specifically requested, and will not notify the payor of such amounts. Any request for refund must be filed within two years from the date the fee was paid (see exceptions below). If the payor does not provide banking information for EFT refunds or instructions to credit a deposit account, the Office may require such information or may use banking info on the payment instrument; refunds of credit card payments will be credited to the charged credit card account. Refund requests based on a deposit account charge must include a copy of the deposit account statement and are subject to a two-year filing period measured from the statement date in certain situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refunds for reexamination and supplemental examination requests
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Director decides not to institute a reexamination or supplemental examination proceeding, certain fees paid with the request will be refunded or returned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For ex parte reexamination, the ex parte reexamination filing fee paid by the requester, less the fee set forth in § 1.20(c)(7), will be refunded. For inter partes reexamination, a refund of $7,970 will be made to the requester if the Director decides not to institute the proceeding. For a supplemental examination request, the fee for reexamination ordered as a result of supplemental examination (per § 1.20(k)(2)) will be returned to the patent owner if the Director decides not to institute reexamination. Refunds generally will be issued in the form of the original payment (e.g., credit back to the credit card). The requester or patent owner should indicate the form in which any refund should be made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refund timing and special rules (deposit accounts and small entity status)
rubrics_metrics.description: Time periods and start-dates for refund requests vary by payment method and circumstance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General refund request period is two years from payment date. For refunds based upon deposit account charges where the Office charged an amount other than specified on the authorization, the two-year refund period begins on the date of the deposit account statement indicating the charge. For refunds based on later establishment of small entity status under 37 CFR 1.28(a), the applicant has three months from the date the charge authorization is received in the Office (receipt date for deposit-account charges) to request a refund. These time periods are non-extendable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refund of search fee and excess claims fee upon express abandonment petition
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may refund the search fee and any excess claims fee paid in an application filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) if applicant files a petition under 37 CFR 1.138(d) to expressly abandon the application before an examination has been made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 711.01 for further practice. The basic filing fee, non-electronic filing fee, examination fee, and application size fee cannot be refunded unless paid by mistake or in excess of that required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification disclosure requirement (35 U.S.C. 112(a) / 37 CFR 1.71)
rubrics_metrics.description: To obtain a valid patent, the application as filed must contain a full and clear disclosure of the invention as prescribed by 35 U.S.C. 112(a). The specification must include a written description of the invention and of the manner and process of making and using the same, in such full, clear, concise, and exact terms as to enable any person skilled in the art to make and use the invention (37 CFR 1.71(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The specification must set forth the precise invention and distinguish it from the prior art, describe a specific embodiment, and explain the mode of operation when applicable. The best mode contemplated by the inventor must be set forth. If a newly filed application obviously fails to disclose the invention with the clarity required, revision should be required. All amendments and claims must find descriptive basis in the original disclosure; no new matter may be introduced after filing. The written description must not include information unrelated to the invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification requirements for improvements
rubrics_metrics.description: In the case of an improvement, the specification must particularly point out the part(s) of the process, machine, manufacture, or composition of matter to which the improvement relates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The description should be confined to the specific improvement and to such parts as necessarily cooperate with it or are necessary to a complete understanding or description of it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decorum and prohibition of offensive language or drawings (37 CFR 1.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an examiner notes the use of language that could be deemed offensive to any race, religion, sex, ethnic group, or nationality, he or she should object to the use of the language as failing to comply with 37 CFR 1.3, which proscribes presentation of papers lacking in decorum and courtesy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inclusion of such proscribed language or offensive drawings should be objected to. An application should not be classified for publication or passed to issue until such language or drawings have been deleted or propriety fully resolved. See MPEP § 714.25 for amendments and papers presented in violation of 37 CFR 1.3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification and related sections must begin on separate sheets/pages
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification must commence on a separate sheet. The claim(s), abstract, and "Sequence Listing" (if required) should not be included on a sheet including any other part of the application (37 CFR 1.71(f)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims, abstract, and sequence listing should each begin on a new page because each is separately indexed in the Image File Wrapper. There should be no overlap on a single page of more than one section of the disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retention and amendment of specification; cross-references
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification is never returned to applicant; applicants should retain accurate copies. Certain cross-references to related applications may be made, but references identified only by attorney docket number should be canceled or amended to properly identify earlier applications (see 37 CFR 1.78).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the attorney or applicant amends the specification, compliance with 37 CFR 1.121 is required. Form paragraph practice and requirements for amendments (e.g., names in joint research agreements) are provided, including processing fee and timing rules for certain amendments (see 37 CFR 1.71(g)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of form paragraphs for minor informalities
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph 7.29 may be used where the disclosure contains minor informalities; form paragraphs 6.29-6.31 should be used where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of minor informalities: spelling errors, inconsistent terminology, numbering of elements. Specific form paragraphs address spacing of lines (¶6.29), numerous errors in specification (¶6.30), and lengthy specification (¶6.31). Examiners should use these paragraphs to point out minor informalities and request corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper quality, size, margins, and physical requirements (37 CFR 1.52(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers to become part of the permanent USPTO records must be on sheets that are flexible, strong, smooth, non-shiny, durable, and white; either DIN A4 (21.0 × 29.7 cm) or 8 1/2 × 11 inches (21.6 × 27.9 cm); with specified top/side/right/bottom margins.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each sheet must include a top margin of at least 2.0 cm (3/4 inch), left side margin at least 2.5 cm (1 inch), right side margin at least 2.0 cm, bottom margin at least 2.0 cm. Papers should have no holes in the sheets as submitted. Pre-printed Office forms and certain double-column reissue copies are exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Text font, single-column, one-sided, legibility and printing (37 CFR 1.52(a)(2)-(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Text must be written on only one side in portrait orientation, in a nonscript type font (e.g., Arial, Times Roman, or Courier), preferably font size 12; capital letters should be at least 0.3175 cm (0.125 inch) high but not smaller than 0.21 cm (0.08 inch). Only a single column of text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text should be plainly and legibly written by typewriter or machine printer in permanent dark ink or equivalent, and presented with sufficient clarity and contrast to permit direct reproduction (photographic, electrostatic, photo-offset, microfilming, and electronic capture).

rubrics_metrics.name: Spacing, page numbering, and paragraph numbering rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification lines should be 1 1/2 or double spaced; pages of the specification including claims and abstract must be numbered consecutively starting with 1; paragraphs (other than claims/abstract) may be numbered at filing and should use Arabic numerals with at least four numerals enclosed in square brackets (e.g., [0001]) and highlighted in bold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraph numbers should appear to the right of the left margin as the first item in each paragraph, followed by a gap. Nontext elements (tables, formulae, sequence data) are considered part of the numbered paragraph around or above them and should not be independently numbered. Paragraph or section headers are not considered paragraphs and should not be numbered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language and translation requirements for non-English filings
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications may be filed in a language other than English, but different requirements apply depending on type of application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For nonprovisional applications under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) filed in a language other than English, an English translation, a statement that the translation is accurate, and the processing fee (37 CFR 1.17(i)) are required; if not filed the applicant will be notified and given time to file or face abandonment. For provisional applications (35 U.S.C. 111(b)) filed in a language other than English, an English translation is not required in the provisional application. See § 1.78(a) for claiming benefit of a provisional in a nonprovisional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read-only optical disc submission requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Electronic documents submitted on a read-only optical disc that are to become part of the permanent USPTO record must comply with specific rules (37 CFR 1.52(e)). Permitted documents include Computer Program Listing Appendices, Sequence Listings, Sequence Listing XML, and Large Tables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read-only discs must be finalized and conform to ISO 9660 and be CD–ROM/CD–R or DVD–R/DVD+R. Discs must be PC or Mac compatible; contents must be ASCII plain text (or XML for Sequence Listing XML) and if compressed must follow applicable §§ (1.58, 1.96, 1.824, 1.834). Each disc must be enclosed in a hard case within an unsealed padded envelope and accompanied by a transmittal letter including: first-named inventor, title, attorney docket, application number/filing date (if known), operating system used, and list of files with size and creation date. Each disc must have a permanent label with inventor, title, docket, application number/filing date, date recorded, and disc order. Discs will not be returned and may not be retained as part of the application file. Amendments require replacement discs per cited sections. The specification must contain an incorporation by reference paragraph identifying each file, date of creation, and size in bytes (except international stage). Unreadable files are treated as not submitted and will prompt a notice to require a compliant submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments and replacement of read-only optical discs
rubrics_metrics.description: Any amendment to the information on a read-only optical disc must be by way of a replacement read-only optical disc, complying with relevant sections for that document type (§ 1.58 for Large Tables, § 1.96 for Computer Program Listing Appendix, § 1.825 for Sequence Listing, § 1.835 for Sequence Listing XML).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replacement disc must comply with the same formatting, enclosure, transmittal, and labeling requirements; unreadable files are treated as not submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determining application size fees for submissions on read-only discs or via EFS
rubrics_metrics.description: The MPEP addresses how application size fees are to be determined for applications containing electronic documents submitted either on read-only optical discs or via the USPTO patent electronic filing system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text begins rules for submission on read-only optical discs and promises a framework for calculating application size fees for such submissions (see MPEP § 1.58 and related provisions). Examiners and filers should follow the specific subsection instructions (f)(1) and subsequent paragraphs for fee determination.
